title: Sidecar Ingress Overlay Terraform Upgrade Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook documents the planned upgrade to introduce an ingress-overlay pattern that uses a lightweight sidecar proxy per tenant overlay network. Goals: reduce blast radius for ingress routing, allow per-tenant L7 rules without cluster-wide gateway churn, and make Terraform module changes predictable for private/VPC deployments.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies only to Private deployments (VPC and on-prem package).
- Changes touch: terraform modules for ingress (module.ingress), networking overlay (module.overlay_net), private-dns glue (module.dns-private), NAT behavior, and cilent-side networkpolicy templates.
- No customer data plane change expected; we aim for zero-downtime upgrades but allow short reconnection windows during canary.
- Must be compatible with existing HAProxy/Envoy ingress gateways for sites that are not on overlay.

High-level approach:
1) Introduce new Terraform module inputs that are additive (feature flags) so we can deploy without changing behavior: enable_sidecar_overlay = false by default.
2) Implement sidecar injection and overlay network CRDs/templates as opt-in.
3) Run canaries in a single non-prod customer VPC; verify connectivity, metrics, and DNS resolution.
4) Gradually flip feature flag per VPC (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
5) Remove legacy toggle after 2 release cycles once stable.

Modules & variables (notes for infra engineers):
- module.ingress (modules/ingress): new var enable_sidecar_overlay (bool), sidecar_image (string), sidecar_resources (map), overlay_annotation_key (string).
- module.overlay_net (modules/overlay_net): new resources for ip-ip tunnel or vxlan, var overlay_backend = ["vxlan","wireguard"]; default = "vxlan". Requires cross-subnet MTU check.
- module.dns-private: add stub resolver override template: attribute "stub_resolver_servers" (list) and per-tenant search-suffix injection.
- module.nat (modules/nat): add var hairpin_enabled (bool) and egress-affinity_label (string).
- module.network_policies: param ingress_sidecar_namespace_label to auto-generate tighter policies for overlay workloads.

Terraform upgrade workflow (detailed):
Preflight (local):
- git checkout infra/ingress-overlay-upgrade branch.
- terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-terraform-state-prod" -reconfigure
- terraform validate
- terraform workspace select <vpc-workspace> || terraform workspace new <vpc-workspace>
- Run terraform plan -var='enable_sidecar_overlay=false' -out=tfplan.before
- Save current state snapshot (aws s3 cp statefile statefile.bak) and tag with timestamp.

Canary (non-prod customer):
- Set enable_sidecar_overlay=true for workspace pointing to the canary VPC.
- terraform apply -var='enable_sidecar_overlay=true' -auto-approve
- Wait for overlay_net resources to be created and sidecar image deployed to target namespaces.
- Verify no iptable conflicts on hosts (run agent-collector host-check script).

Verification checklist (canary):
- DNS: dig @<stub_resolver> my-service.tenant.svc.cluster.local -> returns tenant-private IPs.
- Ingress routing: curl -H 'Host: my-service.tenant.redwood' http://<ingress-proxy> -> 200 with X-Tenant header set.
- Sidecar to backend: curl to local pod IP: connection ok, latency baseline within 15% of previous.
- NAT hairpin: service in same VPC calling public endpoint should loopback correctly (test script run: ./tests/hairpin-check.sh).
- Network policies: kubectl get networkpolicy -n tenant-foo -> ensure deny-by-default exists and sidecar is allowed.
- Observability: Prometheus queries: 
  - envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_total{cluster="sidecar_inbound"} >= 1
  - k8s_service_errors_total{tenant="canary"} == 0
- Logs: sidecar ready logs no repeated 5xxs for 10 minutes.

Rollback plan (canary and per-VPC rollout):
- If any of the verification checks fail, run: terraform apply -var='enable_sidecar_overlay=false' -auto-approve
- Restore previous terraform state snapshot if state drift is detected: aws s3 cp statefile.bak statefile && terraform refresh
- If overlay components have partially created cloud resources (tunnels), run the cleanup target: terraform destroy -target=module.overlay_net -auto-approve

Staged rollout plan (prod VPCs):
- Phase A (10%): pick low-traffic VPCs (region staging customers). Flip flag, monitor 24h.
- Phase B (50%): ramp to business-critical but low-concurrency VPCs. Monitor 72h.
- Phase C (100%): remaining VPCs. Keep toggle in place for 2 weeks for safety.

Operational checklist for each VPC before flip:
- Confirm IPAM ranges for overlay do not overlap customer CIDRs.
- Confirm MTU >= 1400 on all dataplane interfaces (overlay fragmentation risk).
- Confirm no host-level iptables rules that drop vxlan/udp encaps (ports 4789).
- Confirm node OS kernel supports required sysctls for tunnel (sufficient version).
- Confirm KMS access for any secrets used by sidecar image.

Observability and alerting additions:
- New dashboards in Redwood Console: "Ingress Overlay - per VPC" showing: sidecar availability, per-tenant 95th latency, error budget burn, DNS lookup latencies.
- Alerts: Alert if sidecar_restart_rate > 5 / 5m or if dns_lookup_latency_p50 > 200ms for > 10m.
- Tracing: ensure span name contains overlay=true tag; update Jaeger sampling to include 10% of overlay requests.

Testing harness and smoke tests:
- Add new test cases to infra/tests/ingress_overlay_smoke (go), included in nightly:
  - tenant DNS resolution tests
  - end-to-end request path (ingress->sidecar->backend) validated under load (k6 script)
  - hairpin and cross-subnet checks
- Local debug: kubectl port-forward svc/ingress-proxy 8080:80 and run curl with X-Tenant header for rapid repro.

Security considerations:
- Sidecar image must be scanned and signed by CI; image tag pinned in terraform var sidecar_image.
- Network policies must be default deny for pods; explicit allow only for sidecar and control plane.
- Avoid exposing nodePorts for overlay traffic; use hostRoutes only when necessary.

Open questions / risks to resolve before Phase B:
- Wireguard vs VXLAN tradeoffs in cross-data-center networks (performance vs MTU).
- Impact on private-dns cache TTL and stub_resolver scaling for high tenant counts.
- How to surface per-tenant routing metrics without high cardinality explosion.

Rollback runbook (commands):
- To flip a tenant back quickly:
  1) terraform workspace select <tenant-vpc>
  2) terraform apply -var='enable_sidecar_overlay=false' -auto-approve
  3) kubectl -n tenant-<id> rollout restart deployment/ingress-sidecar || kubectl delete pods -l app=ingress-sidecar
  4) Run ./tests/verify-basic-connectivity.sh <tenant-vpc>

Post-upgrade tidy:
- After 2 stable release cycles: remove enable_sidecar_overlay flag and merge sidecar codepath as default.
- Consolidate overlay module outputs into module.ingress outputs for simpler consumption.
- Document changes in customer upgrade notes for Private package.

Appendix - Helpful commands and snippets:
- Check MTU across nodes: ssh node && ip link show | grep mtu
- Dig test: dig +short @10.10.0.2 mysvc.tenant.svc.cluster.local
- Terraform plan example: terraform plan -var='enable_sidecar_overlay=true' -out=tfplan.canary
- Destroy overlay target: terraform destroy -target=module.overlay_net -auto-approve

Notes / author commentary:
- This playbook prioritizes safety via feature flags and per-VPC workspaces. The overlay pattern reduces gateway surface area but increases per-node complexity; expect some host-level debugging initially.
- Keep communications ready for customers who run their own on-prem networking teams: provide MTU guide and firewall port list (vxlan 4789, wireguard 51820 UDP).

TODOs before this doc becomes final:
- Add exact CI job names that will gate sidecar image promotion.
- Add customer-facing release note draft with migration checklist.
- Produce an SRE runbook variant that strips developer-level debugging steps and leaves only ops commands.
